crop.notes: Whole article in three pieces, from headline decks to closing rule.

ocr.notes: Minor slips: 'who is up in New York' should be 'who is now in New York'; 'whip him too' is printed 'to'; Coburn says 'he don't mean business' (OCR 'doesn't'); the 'ALLEN CHALLENGES COBURN.' subhead is omitted.

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Evening Dispatch reported that Allen, in Chicago, telegraphed that Joe Goss was not in America and offered to fight Joe Coburn with gloves for any money; Coburn called it an advertising dodge.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'St. Louis Dispatch, Monday Evening, April 17, 1876'; filed as the Evening Dispatch per rubric (pre-1878-12).

facts.fact: Allen was in Chicago, appearing at the Chicago Adelphi, amid rumors he had left St. Louis to avoid Joe Coburn
Allen telegraphed the Dispatch from Chicago that Joe Goss was not in the country and that the story was got up by Coburn and his friends
facts.quote: I learn that Joe Goss is not in this country, as reported. This story was gotten up by Joe Coburn and his friends.

facts.fact: Allen challenged Joe Coburn to a glove fight for all the money Coburn could get; Coburn refused, calling it an advertising dodge, and offered only to fight for fun without gloves in St. Louis
facts.quote: Say through the DISPATCH for me, that I will fight Coburn with the gloves for all the money he can get.

facts.fact: Jem Mace wrote to Coburn that Joe Goss had come to America on a special mission to fight Allen (Allen denied Goss was in the country)
